On 11 September 2001 nineteen hijackers of al-Qaeda seized four airliners in the United States. Two were flown into the twin towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, which collapsed, one into the Pentagon near Washington, and one crashed in a field in Pennsylvania after passengers fought back.

Nearly 3,000 people were killed, the deadliest terrorist attack in history. The plot was directed by Osama bin Laden.

Within weeks the United States and its allies invaded Afghanistan to overthrow the Taliban, who sheltered al-Qaeda. The attacks led to the Iraq War of 2003, new security at airports, mass surveillance, and the prison at Guantanamo Bay. Bin Laden was killed by US forces in 2011.
